nodes.line: Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

I'll be straight with you. I start at five in the morning and for a month the Turrella back lane has had somebody in it who is not waiting for bread. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. You'll know it when you see it.

It has been three weeks. A light on that lane costs Turrella $52 and the landlord has said no twice, so we are doing it ourselves. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: five in the morning at Turrella — that's done.
The Lane Light, Turrella — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

Nobody else has offered, so. The flour for Turrella comes off a truck at five in the morning and last Thursdays the truck came and the flour did not. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

The council knows and the council does not care. The Turrella loading zone has had a car in it at five in the morning every morning this week and the driver waits in it, which makes it worse. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. I would rather know than wonder.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: The Loading Zone, Turrella — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Mirza, front of house at Turrella

nodes.line: Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Somebody two doors down from Turrella put up a sign on Thursdays that says the same six words as ours, in the same order. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. That's the whole job. No catch.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. This business was at Arncliffe before it was at Turrella, and there is a woman there who still has the original book. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.
I had a feeling. Go on.

choices.text: The Sourdough Sign, Turrella — that's done.
The Old Site, Turrella — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

I'll be straight with you. Council has been saying the Royal Randwick pool is at end of life since the week of the show and the crack they keep pointing at is not in the shell. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. You'll know it when you see it.

It has been three weeks. We are running a stall for Royal Randwick on the week of the show and a stall needs $95 of gear that nobody has volunteered to pay for. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Royal Randwick Pool — that's done.
The Petition Stall, Royal Randwick — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Charlie, swim coach at Royal Randwick

nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

Nobody else has offered, so. I coach 24 kids at Royal Randwick at the middle of the news and three of them have stopped coming without anybody ringing me. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

The council knows and the council does not care. A group has been coming over the Royal Randwick fence after close and swimming in the dark, which is how Royal Randwick loses its pool. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. I would rather know than wonder.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Deep End, Royal Randwick — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.

npcs.name: Sigrid, kiosk operator at Royal Randwick

nodes.line: Ah. Someone with two working legs.

I have been putting it off since Easter. The kiosk at Royal Randwick has a chest freezer that hums in D in it and a freezer that has been running warm since the week of the show. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. That's the whole job. No catch.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. They want everyone from Royal Randwick to drive to the new centre at UNSW Anzac Parade, so somebody should go and see whether it is any good. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Kiosk Freezer, Royal Randwick — that's done.
The Aquatic Centre, Royal Randwick — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Xuan, taxi driver at Bardwell Park

nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

I'll be straight with you. The rank outside Bardwell Park used to hold nine cars and since a public holiday nobody remembered it holds four, and nobody will say who moved the line. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. You'll know it when you see it.

It has been three weeks. Since the rank at Bardwell Park shrank I am $68 a week down, and the association wants that number from somebody who can prove it. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Bardwell Park Rank — that's done.
Lost Fares, Bardwell Park — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.

npcs.name: Sigrid, rank marshal at Bardwell Park

nodes.line: Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

Nobody else has offered, so. Cars that have never sat in the Bardwell Park queue turn up at half six and take the front of it, and the drivers who waited say nothing. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

The council knows and the council does not care. When the last train into Bardwell Park is late, 88 people come out at once and I have to have cars there before they do. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. I would rather know than wonder.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: Queue Jumpers, Bardwell Park — that's done.
The Late Train, Bardwell Park — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Sakura, hotel doorman at Bardwell Park

nodes.line: Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

I have been putting it off since Easter. I have stood on this door near Bardwell Park for 88 years and since a public holiday nobody remembered somebody has been sending my guests to a different rank. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. That's the whole job. No catch.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. The plates working the Bardwell Park rank are dispatched from a depot at Turrella, and the man who runs it has never met a driver he liked. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: The Door, Bardwell Park — that's done.
The Depot, Bardwell Park — that's done.
